clarification_rounds.question: What kind of pressure do you want to practise under — deciding which of several inbound threats to engage first, or something else?
When you say yes — do you want several threats arriving at once and too few missiles to cover them all?

scenario_instance.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Sequenced Kill Chain, Sector North-East
scenario_instance.situation_brief:
You are the console operator at a fixed ground-based air-defence site. Your radar does not rotate: it holds a 120-degree sector centred on 040 degrees, and you own the tilt inside it. Detection depends on class — fast fixed-wing out to 150 km, rotary-wing to 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km. Engagement rings are 70 km long, 50 km medium, 20 km short, with a 5 km inner limit.

Higher formation warns of a coordinated push against this site inside the next four minutes. Expect mixed composition arriving in overlapping waves. Own aviation and allied movements are active in the same airspace and may enter the sector without prior correlation.

Hard system limit: no more than two rockets may be in the air at once. A third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Track classification of an unresolved contact is referred to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds; nothing may be fired on unless it stands as Enemy. The console auto-types tracks and its type call is not always right — check speed and altitude against the type before you commit.

The launchers are cold and both are yours. Work the picture.

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer. Crosses the 70 km ring at roughly t+22 s; first valid firing solution of the run.
Second fast closer, offset right of the lead. Reaches the 70 km ring at roughly t+67 s.
Low and fastest of the three. Enters the long ring near t+116 s, coincident with the heaviest part of the unmanned wave.
Already inside the medium ring at detection; presents a valid solution from the first sweep and will tempt an early launcher commitment.
Steady inbound on the left shoulder of the sector.
Right-flank entry while both jets are likely being serviced.
Faster than the earlier unmanned tracks; will cross the 20 km ring first if left unserviced.
Console auto-types this contact as a jet; speed and altitude do not support that call. Operator should correct the type before selecting an interceptor.
Low on the extreme right edge of the sector; may need tilt attention to hold a solution.
Tail of the wave, lowest and fastest unmanned track. Arrives only if the queue has been kept moving.
Low, slow, inbound. Never resolves unaided — classification must be referred. Sits near the tilt floor and may fade in and out of the picture.
High-level transit crossing the sector rather than closing. Resolves late and unaided at t+130 s if not referred sooner.

Fast, low, closing directly on the site with heading and altitude changes that read as aggressive. Crosses the 70 km ring near t+115 s and never resolves unaided. The single most dangerous track on the display for the wrong reason.

success_criteria.statement: Win by destroying all three fast closers at the earliest valid firing solution each offers, then clearing the unmanned wave by earliest available solution inside the shorter rings, all within 240 seconds. Every unresolved track must be referred for classification and none may be fired on unless it stands as Enemy. Firing on an Unknown or a friendly fails the run outright, whatever the kill count. One leaked unmanned track is tolerable; a leaked jet is not. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction.
